tool.name: Babylon.js Editor
tool.installMode: copied .app to /tmp, launched without system-wide install; quarantine flag not modified

experiment.saveMethod: Editor MCP endpoint save_scene (confirmation dialog accepted in the Editor UI)
experiment.automation: Renderer driven through the Editor's own remote debugging port (8315); MCP HTTP server started on 127.0.0.1:3712

fileFormat.layout: One directory per scene (assets/<name>.scene). Inside: cameras/, lights/, meshes/, geometries/, shadowGenerators/, config.json, preview.png. Each object is a separate JSON file named by its UUID; geometry payloads are separate binary files.

firstSaveAfterAddingObjects.note: The template declares version 5.0.0 and was saved by 5.5.2, so existing JSON gained/changed default fields and key order. This is one-time upgrade churn, not per-save noise.

noOpSave.note: Saving again without edits leaves the working tree clean.

moveOneObject.note: A real object edit produces a one-line JSON diff; only the regenerated preview thumbnail is binary noise.

diffNoiseSources: preview.png is regenerated on every save (binary thumbnail, not needed for runtime).
Geometry payloads (*.babylonbinarymeshdata) and environment/image assets are binary and cannot be line-diffed.
Object/scene files are named by UUID; reviewers must read the name field inside JSON to identify an object.
First save after an Editor/Babylon version upgrade rewrites defaults and key order across existing JSON files.

conclusion.rationale: Scene data is stored as one human-readable JSON file per object with stable key order and idempotent saves. A single object edit is a one-line text diff. The remaining noise is limited to the generated preview.png and expected binary geometry/asset payloads, which can be handled with .gitignore, Git LFS or an export step.
recommendations: Keep the Babylon.js Editor + Node Geometry dual-track plan; do not trigger the LDtk fallback for git-friendliness reasons.
Use Git LFS (or ignore regenerable exports) for *.babylonbinarymeshdata, *.env, PNG/JPEG if the repository grows.
Pin the Editor version per project and avoid mixing Editor versions in one branch to prevent one-time default/key-order churn.
When reviewing, use the JSON name field rather than the UUID filename to locate an object; a generated index file could be added later if needed.

notes: The Editor was launched from a copied .app under /tmp with DEBUG=true because it was automated headlessly; this changed Havok's WASM lookup path, so the preview engine had to be initialized manually. This is an automation detail, not a project-format limitation.
The first launch without DEBUG showed the dashboard; the project was opened through the Editor's IPC channel after setting the editor app path.
The full 998MB app and the 232MB project node_modules stay outside the repository; only report, screenshots and small samples are committed.
